confirmedFindings.summary: Acceptance criterion 6's invariant that the suspension transition must NOT disarm a scheduled downgrade has no test, so the fourth transitionAndEmit site is unpinned.
confirmedFindings.detail: Three of the four `transitionAndEmit` call sites in billing.service.ts now perform a gated disarm (555 onCheckoutCompleted, 617 onPaymentSucceeded, 692 onSubscriptionDeleted); only the suspension site at :792 must not. Nothing asserts that. Concrete regression scenario: a later editor, seeing 3 of 4 sites disarm, adds `if (suspended) await this.prisma.tenantSubscription.update({ where: { tenantId: sub.tenantId }, data: disarmedDowngrade() })` inside suspendOverdueTenants (a plausible 'symmetry' change, and the file-local helper now makes it a one-liner). Every test still passes — I ran the full lane: 16 suites / 266 tests green, and the two existing suspendOverdueTenants tests (spec:175-196) only assert `tx.tenant.updateMany` and the -373 delta, never `prisma.tenantSubscription.update`; the new pins T4/T5 only cover the two reinstatement handlers. The resulting behavior is B216 mirrored: a tenant whose payment goes overdue loses the downgrade it legitimately scheduled while ACTIVE, so after reinstatement applyScheduledDowngrades (billing-cron.service.ts:121-176) has nothing to apply and the tenant keeps being billed at the higher basePriceSnapshot. Note the DRY variant (hoisting the disarm into transitionAndEmit itself) IS caught today, because it would make the disarm the first tenantSubscription.update in onSubscriptionDeleted and break spec:128-140 — so only the suspension-site-only change slips through.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Add one pin inside the existing B216 describe (which already has `disarmCall` in scope), e.g. `it("pin B216: suspending an overdue tenant leaves a scheduled downgrade armed", ...)` using `make({ sub: armedSub({ stripeSubId: "sub_1" }), stripeStatus: "unpaid", transitionCount: 1 })`, `await svc.suspendOverdueTenants()`, `expect(disarmCall(prisma)).toBeUndefined()`. Note make()'s `tenantSubscription.findMany` mock already forces `stripeSubId: "sub_1"` on the returned row, so the cron picks it up. No production code change.
